reviews.summary: Reviewers like the easy-to-use interface, employee scheduling, time tracking, team messaging, and integrated payroll features. Reviewers complain about app glitches and slow support responses, along with limited payroll features, billing problems, and notification issues.

pricing.note: Homebase has a free Basic plan for one location with up to 10 employees, with paid plans of $30 (Essentials), $70 (Plus) and $120 (All-in-One) per location per month, or $24, $56 and $96 per location per month when billed annually.
pricing.extraFees: Payroll is an add-on at a $49 monthly base fee plus $6 per active employee paid per month, with the first 6 months free on the Payroll add-on; background checks cost $30 each, Tip Manager is $25 per location per month, Task Manager is $13 per location per month, job post boosts start at $50 per post, and Hiring Assistant starts at $99 per month.

homebase.caution: The free Basic plan is limited to one location and up to 10 employees and has no scheduling beyond 10 days, employee mobile app, or applicant tracking; if you have more than one location or more than 10 employees you need Essentials or higher. If you do not pick a plan after the 14-day All-in-One trial, the account automatically moves to the free Basic plan. Clover-billed customers can't upgrade through Clover anymore since October 2025 and need to contact Homebase support.

description.summary: Homebase is an app for small businesses with hourly teams that combines employee scheduling, time clock tracking, payroll, hiring, and team messaging in one place. It is built for businesses like restaurants, retail shops, and home services.
helpsWith: Build employee schedules, manage shift swaps and time off, and send reminders to your team
Track employee clock-ins and clock-outs from a mobile or tablet time clock, and flag missed punches, breaks, and overtime
Post job openings to job boards like Indeed and Craigslist, and track applicants in one place
Send messages to individuals or groups and see when staff have read their schedules

ai.feature: Builds draft weekly staff schedules, flags timecard errors and overtime risk, screens job applicants, and drafts job posts for a small business owner.

reviews.summary: Users like that Google Translate is simple, fast, free for most everyday needs, and handles text, voice, camera and conversation translation across many languages. Users say translations can be inaccurate or unnatural with idioms, slang, technical or complex text, that some features and voice or conversation modes are buggy, and that privacy and support are weak.

pricing.note: Google Translate is free for personal use on the website and mobile apps, while the Cloud Translation API is pay-as-you-go at $20 per million characters after a free 500,000 characters per month.
pricing.extraFees: Document translation through the API costs $0.08 per page for standard NMT, and custom models cost more, starting at $80 per million characters in one source and $0.25 per page in another; HTML tags and whitespace count as billable characters.

google-translate.caution: The free consumer website and apps have no per-character bill, but the API needs a Google Cloud project with billing enabled and does not share a quota with the website; sources also disagree on custom model pricing, and translated captions in Google Meet are only available on certain Workspace editions.

description.summary: Google Translate is a free tool that translates text, photos of signs or menus, documents, websites and spoken conversations between languages. It works in a web browser and as a phone app, and some features also work without an internet connection.
helpsWith: Hold a two-way conversation where each person speaks and the app translates aloud and on screen
Upload a document to translate it, keeping the original next to the result for checking
Translate a whole webpage by entering its web address

ai.feature: Translates text and live speech between many languages, and explains idioms, slang, and alternative phrasings with Gemini-powered context.

reviews.summary: Reviewers like that Wave is easy to use, has a simple interface, and handles invoicing and expense tracking well for small businesses, with a free core version. Reviewers complain about slow or missing customer support, delayed or held payment transfers, limited reporting and advanced features, and the cost of paid upgrades.

pricing.note: The Starter plan is free, and the Pro plan costs $19 per month or $190 billed annually, with optional add-ons such as payroll from $25 per month and a bookkeeper from $149 per month, per waveapps.com.
pricing.extraFees: Online card payments cost 2.9% + $0.60 per transaction on Starter and 3.4% + $0.60 for Amex, while Pro lowers this to 2.9% + $0 for the first ten transactions each month, then 2.9% + $0.60 after that, per waveapps.com.

wave.caution: Approval for online payments depends on identity verification and a credit review, and the Pro subscription fee is charged per business rather than per owner, per waveapps.com. Some integrations such as Amazon, Etsy and eBay are only available to US businesses, per waveapps.com.

description.summary: Wave is accounting software for small businesses that handles bookkeeping and invoicing. A free Starter Plan covers basic accounting and invoicing, and a paid Pro Plan adds more money tools like receipt scanning and automatic bank imports.
description.howToStart: Open the Wave sign-up page on a web browser or install the Wave mobile app, enter your email and a password, enter your business information, and choose the free Starter Plan.

reviews.summary: Reviewers like the ease of use, reliable call quality, call transcripts and recordings, multiple phone lines, and the Slack and Zapier integrations. Reviewers complain about dropped or missed calls, buggy features, a non-intuitive interface, slow support responses, and unreliable call transfers and notifications.}

pricing.note: Quo (formerly OpenPhone) has three per-user plans billed annually: Starter at $15 per month, Business at $23 per month, and Scale at $35 per month, with monthly billing at $19, $33 and $47 per user; there is no permanent free plan, only a 7-day free trial.
pricing.extraFees: Each additional phone number costs $5 per month; US texting requires 10DLC registration with a one-time $19.50 review fee plus a monthly messaging fee of $1.50 to $3 depending on business type; $15 resubmission fee if rejected; international calls and texts are billed per use; Sona AI receptionist includes 10 calls per month, with paid tiers starting at $25 per month for 50 calls; Zapier and Make automated texts cost $0.01 per segment.

openphone.caution: Texting is not available during the free trial and requires registering your number first; international calls and texts are not included in the trial; the Starter plan does not connect to a CRM, so HubSpot and Salesforce integrations need the Business plan or higher.

description.summary: Quo (formerly OpenPhone) is a business phone system that gives you a separate work number on your phone, with calls, texts, and voicemails in one shared place. It also has an AI receptionist that answers calls when you cannot.
helpsWith: Keep work calls and texts separate from your personal number
Get automatic AI summaries and transcripts of phone calls
Share one business number so your team can answer customers together
Send auto-replies to incoming messages when no one is available
description.howToStart: Download the Quo app, create an account to start the free seven-day trial, and choose a local or toll-free number.

ai.feature: Answers missed calls with an AI agent, captures caller details, and summarizes calls and transcripts for follow-up.

pricing.note: The Red Cards are free to download and print from ILRC's site; small businesses can order printed cards from RedCardOrders.com, a union-run printer where you pay the printer directly, and the results do not list a per-card or per-order price.
pricing.extraFees: Businesses and private attorneys ordering printed cards pay the printer directly; prices are on the printer's site and are not stated in the results.

ilrc-red-cards.caution: ILRC warns that some social media posts sell Red Cards; the cards are free, so only download them from ILRC's site, which it says is the only source it checks. ILRC ships free cards only to immigrant-serving nonprofits and public defenders, not to small businesses.

description.summary: The ILRC's Red Cards are small two-sided cards that help people state their rights and protect themselves during encounters with immigration enforcement, such as when ICE agents come to a home. They are free and are available in many languages.
helpsWith: Give staff and customers a card that shows their constitutional rights, which apply to everyone regardless of immigration status
Use cards during Know Your Rights workshops and client appointments, and keep a stack in a waiting room or at the front desk
Print your own cards from free artwork in 59 languages, or order them free through the ILRC if you are a nonprofit

reviews.summary: One reviewer said the service was easy to use, had many features, and helped them get new leads and cut customer service costs. Reviewers complain about surprise price increases, unrefunded charges after cancellation, unanswered billing emails, and sales pitches instead of help when calling customer service.

pricing.note: Goodcall has Starter at $79 per month for 100 unique customers, Growth at $129 per month for 500 unique customers, Scale at $299 per month for 2,000 unique customers, and a custom Enterprise plan, with no free plan beyond a free demo agent that requires a paid plan once you connect a phone number.
pricing.extraFees: Overage beyond included unique customers is $0.79 each on Starter, $0.26 each on Growth, and $0.15 each on Scale; minutes and calls are not metered, and no per-minute, transaction or setup fees are listed.

goodcall.caution: Booking integrations vary: the vendor page names Google Calendar, Google Sheets and HighLevel natively, while ServiceTitan and Housecall Pro are listed as vendor claims, and Jobber connects only via Zapier. Goodcall offers no annual plan currently, and a unique customer is counted once per phone number per month (voice.morshedworx.com, callbotscore.com).

description.summary: Goodcall is an AI phone agent that answers your business calls 24/7, takes the caller's details, and books appointments or sends the lead to your team. You set it up by describing your business in plain words, and it can also run from your website details.
helpsWith: Answers calls at night, on weekends, and when your main line is busy, using your business information
Takes down the caller's details and sends you the lead by text and email as the call ends
Books appointments into Google Calendar and transfers to a person when needed
description.howToStart: Build your agent by describing your business, test it with practice calls, then pick a phone number and forward your existing line to it.

reviews.summary: Users like that it is secure, syncs reliably across devices, offers a strong free tier, and makes generating and storing complex passwords easy. Users dislike the dated or unpolished interface, inconsistent autofill and autosave, some advanced features being limited to paid plans, and login errors reported by some App Store users.

pricing.note: Bitwarden has a free plan, a Premium individual plan at $1.65 per month billed annually, a Families plan at $3.99 per month billed annually, a Teams plan at $4 per user per month billed annually, and an Enterprise plan billed per user, which Capterra reports at $6 per user per month, with custom quotes for large organizations.
pricing.extraFees: Taxes are not included in the listed prices. Secrets Manager is an optional add-on with an additional fee for Teams and Enterprise organizations.

bitwarden.caution: Prices shown are based on annual billing, and Premium individual and Families plans are billed annually only. Teams and Enterprise can be billed monthly or annually. Enterprise is priced per user and is listed by reviewers at $6 per user per month, which differs from the vendor page's blank figure, so confirm the current Enterprise rate with Bitwarden before buying. The free plan allows one user, and a Free organization allows only two users and two collections.

description.summary: Bitwarden is a password manager that stores, creates and fills in strong, unique passwords for all your accounts, so you only need to remember one master password. It works on computers and phones and can be used by small businesses to share logins safely.
helpsWith: Create and store a different strong password for every website and app, so one hacked account does not expose the others
Share logins with coworkers or your team securely through business plans
Fill in logins and cards automatically on your phone, computer and browser
Get alerts when a stored password appears in a data breach and needs changing

ai.feature: Lets AI assistants you connect securely access, generate, and manage your Bitwarden passwords, and lets admins run common account tasks through plain-language commands.

reviews.summary: Users like that it is free, easy to use, and helps customers find the business and see photos, reviews, and contact details. Users complain about slow or unclear updates and edits, unpredictable automated suspensions and verification, hard-to-reach or unhelpful customer support, and difficulty removing fake reviews.

pricing.note: Creating, verifying and managing a Google Business Profile is free with no paid or premium tier, while Google Ads and Local Services Ads are optional paid add-ons billed per click or per lead.
pricing.extraFees: Optional Google Ads are billed per click at auction-set prices, Local Services Ads are billed per qualified lead, and third-party listing-management tools charge subscription fees; none are required for the profile.

google-business-profile.caution: Anyone asking for payment to set up, verify, renew or fix a Google Business Profile is not from Google and is likely a scam. Management services from freelancers or agencies typically cost $300 to $2,000 or more per location per month, though the profile itself is free. Sources: business.google.com, optuno.com, ynexgen.com

description.summary: Google Business Profile is a free tool that lets a business manage how it appears on Google Search and Maps, including hours, contact details, photos and reviews. It helps local customers find you and contact you.
helpsWith: Appear when people search for businesses like yours on Google Maps and Search, with your location, hours and contact info
Reply to customer reviews, which show as 'Response from the owner'
Post offers, promotions, announcements and new photos
Show your products, services and menu, and let customers order or book when offered

ai.feature: Lets owners manage their Business Profile through Gemini, drafting replies to reviews, creating posts, summarizing customer feedback, and checking performance insights.

reviews.summary: Users like the accurate, natural-sounding translations, the context and tone handling, and the clean, simple interface. Users dislike the strict free-version limits, app crashes and freezing, declining translation quality after updates, weak support, and poor voice playback.

pricing.note: The free plan gives 50,000 characters per month, one file translation up to 5 MB, and one glossary; paid Individual is $8.74 per month billed annually, Team is $28.74 per user per month annually, and Business is $57.49 per user per month annually, with monthly billing about 16% higher.
pricing.extraFees: Write Pro add-on costs $7.49 per user per month on Individual and Team plans; DeepL API is a separate product with a free Developer tier of 1M characters total, and Growth at $26 per month annually plus usage fees of $27.50 per 1M characters over the included amount.

deepl.caution: Business and Enterprise plans advertise unlimited characters but are subject to a fair usage policy with no published hard cap; the API is billed separately from Translator subscriptions.

description.summary: DeepL is an AI translation tool for text and files, such as Word, PDF and PowerPoint documents, with a free version and paid Pro plans. It keeps the original layout of translated files.
helpsWith: Translate Word, PDF and PowerPoint files while keeping their formatting and layout
Choose a formal or informal tone for your translation
Keep product and industry terms consistent with a glossary
Translate text and images, such as signs or menus

ai.feature: Translates text, documents, and spoken conversations between languages using its own AI language models, and offers AI writing help and an autonomous agent that handles business tasks.

reviews.summary: Users like the natural-sounding human voices, the ease of use, the wide voice library and voice cloning, and the value for the money. Users dislike the confusing credit system that burns through credits quickly, high costs and subscription fees, glitches and lost work without auto-save, slow latency, and billing or account problems.

pricing.note: A free plan gives 10,000 credits a month (about 10 minutes of text to speech) with no commercial license; paid plans are Starter at $6 a month ($5 billed yearly), Creator at $22 ($18.33 yearly), Pro at $99 ($82.50 yearly), Scale at $299, Business at $990, and Enterprise on quote.
pricing.extraFees: Prices exclude taxes, levies and duties. API usage is billed separately per character or per minute (for example $0.08 per 1,000 characters for text to speech), and Pay As You Go lets you prepay for API use. Additional agent minutes on Creator and above bill at $0.08 per minute.

elevenlabs.caution: The free plan has no commercial license, so audio cannot be used commercially; unused credits roll over only on paid plans and are forfeited on downgrade or cancellation. Starter and Creator first-month promotional prices are shown in the results and renew at standard prices. Results do not name other specific app integrations beyond Twilio, and the cited pricing pages were read on October 30, 2026 and may have changed.

description.summary: ElevenLabs turns typed text into natural-sounding speech for ads, videos, audiobooks and phone messages. It also offers sound effects, music and video dubbing for small businesses.
helpsWith: Turn a written script into a voiceover for a short advert or social media video
Create an on-hold or out-of-hours voicemail greeting and download it as an audio file
Translate and dub a video into other languages while keeping the speaker's tone

ai.feature: Answers customer calls, chats, and texts around the clock and books appointments on the business calendar.

reviews.summary: Users like the easy-to-use interface, the large template library, and the drag-and-drop design tools that let non-designers make good graphics quickly. Users dislike that many advanced features, premium templates and AI tools are locked behind a paid subscription, and that the editor lacks advanced vector and typography controls and can lag on large or complex designs.

pricing.note: Canva has a free plan, a Pro plan at US$18 a month or US$180 a year for one person, and a Business plan at US$25 a month or US$250 a year per person, with Enterprise priced by sales.
pricing.extraFees: US sales tax is added where required based on the billing address, and Business is billed per person who accepts an invite.

canva.caution: Canva Teams is no longer available for new sign-ups or upgrades, so a small team today would pick Business. Canva's help center says pricing depends on location, so prices outside the US will differ. The Salesforce app is exclusive to Enterprise.

description.summary: Canva is a web-based design tool that lets small businesses make social media graphics, flyers, menus, presentations and videos using templates and a drag-and-drop editor. It includes AI tools that help create and adapt content.
helpsWith: Create social media graphics, posts and ads from ready-made templates, with pre-set sizes for each platform
Design printable items such as flyers, posters and business cards, and download print-ready files
Use AI tools to write and adapt on-brand content, remove backgrounds and resize designs
Keep logos, colors and fonts in a Brand Kit so your designs stay consistent, with team collaboration on approvals

ai.feature: Generates on-brand designs, images, charts, and captions from a text prompt, applying your brand fonts and colors automatically.

reviews.summary: Users like the easy drag-and-drop editor, customizable templates, and quick setup without coding skills. Users dislike slow loading and lag, template lock-in after publishing, unexpected charges and auto-renewal problems, weak customer support, and confusing pricing.}

pricing.note: Wix has a free plan, then paid plans Light at $17 per month, Core at $29 per month, Business at $39 per month, and Business Elite at $159 per month, all billed yearly.
pricing.extraFees: Wix Payments charges 2.9% plus $0.30 per card transaction in the US, 3.7% plus $0.30 for American Express, and 2.6% for in-person payments. Domain renewals after the first year, around $13.35 per year for.com, and paid apps from the App Market, often $3 to $20+ per month, are extra. Business email runs on Google Workspace, listed at $7 per user per month, billed yearly.

wix.caution: Monthly billing costs more than yearly: Light is $24, Core $36, Business $46 and Business Elite $172 per month. The free plan shows Wix branding, may show ads, and cannot take payments. The free custom domain applies only to a new domain bought from Wix and only in the first year.

description.summary: Wix is a website builder that uses AI to create a complete website from a short description of your business, which you can then edit by hand or with the built-in AI assistant. It also includes business tools such as scheduling, online stores and lead management.
helpsWith: Generate a complete website from a single prompt or a few answers about your business, then adjust text, images, layout and colors
Let clients book appointments through the site with a scheduling tool that syncs with calendar apps
Sell products online and manage inventory, orders and payments from one dashboard
Capture customer inquiries with forms and track them through a sales pipeline

ai.feature: Lets small business owners manage their site and business through AI agents such as Aria, Kleo, Alfred, and Symphony, covering tasks like marketing, answering calls, design, and scheduling.

reviews.summary: Reviewers like its easy setup, affordable pricing, simple interface, and integration with in-person Square sales. Reviewers complain about limited website customization, high or unclear fees, difficult customer support, and limited features for growing businesses.

pricing.note: Square Free is $0 per month per location, Square Plus is $49 per month per location, and Square Premium is $149 per month per location, with Square Pro custom-priced for businesses processing over $250,000 per year.
pricing.extraFees: Free plan processing fees are 3.3% + 30¢ for online payments and 2.6% + 15¢ for tap, dip, or swipe; Plus is 2.9% + 30¢ online and 2.5% + 15¢ in person; Premium is 2.9% + 30¢ online and 2.4% + 15¢ in person.

square-online.caution: Plus and Premium are priced per location, so multiple locations multiply the monthly fee. Plus and Premium include a free 30-day trial, and plans can be cancelled or switched anytime with no locked-in contracts.

description.summary: Square Online lets a small business build a website or online store with no coding and sell products that sync with its in-person Square register. It also includes payments, shipping, pickup and delivery options.
helpsWith: Sell products online that stay synced with in-store sales and inventory across all locations
Offer shipping, in-store pickup, or local delivery for online orders
Let customers create accounts to track orders and get product recommendations
Use built-in SEO tools and social integrations to promote the store
description.howToStart: Create a free Square account, then use the website builder in Square Dashboard to design your store, add products, set up payments and shipping, and publish it.

ai.feature: Rewrites text on your online store with AI, generating alternate versions of a description you write so you can pick one.

reviews.summary: Users like managing Facebook and Instagram from one workspace, scheduling posts in advance, and seeing post performance and audience insights in one place. Users complain about a confusing and frequently changing interface, buggy or failed scheduled posts, delayed messages, no message search, slow customer support, and login problems.

pricing.note: Meta Business Suite is free to use, with no subscription plans; you only pay for any ads you run through it.

meta-business-suite.caution: Meta Verified for business is a separate paid subscription, starting at $14.99 per account per month in the US, and is not part of Business Suite. Ad spend is billed separately from the free platform, and the renewal of Meta Verified is automatic until cancelled.

description.summary: Meta Business Suite is a free workspace that brings your Facebook, Instagram and Messenger business activity into one dashboard. It helps you plan posts, answer messages and check how your content is doing.
helpsWith: Schedule and publish posts and stories to Facebook and Instagram from one calendar
Answer Facebook, Instagram and Messenger messages and comments in one inbox, with saved replies and simple automatic replies
See basic insights on how posts and your audience are performing
Boost posts and create simple ads, with Ads Manager for full campaigns

ai.feature: Answers questions and suggests fixes for your Meta ads, posts, and business data, including ad performance reviews and content planning.

reviews.summary: Users like the clean, intuitive interface, easy scheduling across multiple platforms, and the time it saves on social media management. Users dislike unreliable posting and alerts, multi-image posts failing, limited analytics, high pricing for advanced features, and few details when errors occur.

pricing.note: Free plan covers 3 channels with 10 scheduled posts per channel; Essentials costs $5 per channel per month billed yearly ($6 billed monthly) and Team costs $10 per channel per month billed yearly ($12 billed monthly), so a small business with 5 channels would pay about $25 per month on Essentials or $50 on Team with yearly billing.
pricing.extraFees: No transaction or per-user fees are named in the results; prices are in US dollars and exclude tax.

buffer.caution: The free plan has a lifetime limit of 8 channels per social network, and the free plan's API allowance is 1,000 requests per channel per month. Paid plans bill per channel, so cost grows with each account connected; a 14-day free trial of paid features is offered.

description.summary: Buffer is a social media tool that lets a small business plan, schedule and publish posts to many social accounts from one dashboard, and also shows what content performs well. It also helps reply to comments and reviews from one inbox.
helpsWith: Schedule posts across platforms like Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, LinkedIn and Google Business in advance
Use an AI Assistant to brainstorm ideas, rewrite content and craft platform-specific posts
See simple analytics to learn which posts work best and when to post
Reply to comments and Google Business reviews from one inbox

ai.feature: Generates social media post ideas, rewrites and reformats posts for each platform, and adjusts tone and length, using OpenAI models.

reviews.summary: Users like its powerful targeting, fast setup, high-intent reach to people actively searching, and clear analytics and budget control. Users dislike the steep learning curve, cluttered and changing interface, rising click costs that can overspend budgets, unreliable AI campaigns, and poor customer support and billing disputes.

pricing.note: Google Ads has no free plan or fixed monthly fee; you set your own budget and pay per click, with a typical small US business spending about $500 to $1,000 a month in ad spend, and WordStream's average starting budget being $1,000 to $2,500 a month.
pricing.extraFees: Management fees are billed separately by agencies, with flat monthly fees of about $500 to $5,000 or 10% to 20% of ad spend, and some surcharges by country may apply.

google-ads.caution: Google Ads has no fixed monthly fee, so the real cost is your ad spend plus any agency fees; costs vary widely by industry, and market figures cited here come from third-party sites rather than Google's own pricing page.

description.summary: Google Ads lets a business pay to show its ads on Google Search, Google Maps and other Google sites, so people searching for what it offers can find it. You pay for ads based on clicks or calls, and you set the budget yourself.
helpsWith: Show a map ad that appears when people search or browse nearby on Google Maps
Set a daily or monthly budget cap so you never pay more than you choose
Let Google's AI pick the best combinations of your headlines, images and keywords

ai.feature: Writes ad text, suggests keywords and images, and sets bids to reach searches that match your business.

reviews.summary: Users find the interface intuitive and easy to use, setup is quick, and routine tasks like invoicing and expense tracking are automated. Users say customer support is slow and unhelpful, bank connectivity and reconciliation are unreliable, and reporting and customization are rigid and limited.

pricing.note: Zoho Books has a free plan for 1 user plus an accountant, with paid plans Standard at $15 per org per month, Professional at $40, Premium at $60, Elite at $120 and Ultimate at higher tiers, billed annually, with monthly rates listed in some sources as $20, $50, $70, $150 and $275.
pricing.extraFees: Extra users cost $3 per user per month or $2.50 per user per month billed annually, per the vendor's pricing FAQ; Zoho Payroll and other third-party payroll apps are separate costs.

zoho-books.caution: The free plan stays free only while annual revenue stays under $50K, invoices are capped at 1,000 per year, and sources give different monthly prices for the paid tiers, so check the vendor's current pricing page; Zoho Books does not include built-in payroll and does not connect to many third-party apps compared with competitors.

description.summary: Zoho Books is online accounting software that helps a small business send invoices, track expenses and bank accounts, and see financial reports. It has a free plan for businesses that are just starting out.
helpsWith: Create and send invoices and quotes, and set up payment reminders
Track expenses by scanning receipts and connecting bank accounts
Reconcile bank and card transactions to keep accurate records
View 50+ financial reports, such as profit and loss and balance sheet
description.howToStart: Go to the Zoho Books website, click Sign Up Now, enter your company name, email, phone number and a password, then click Create my account; you can start with the free plan or a 14-day trial of the Premium features.

ai.feature: Answers finance questions and creates invoices, bills, and reports from plain-language prompts, plus drafts reminders and sorts bank transactions.

reviews.summary: Users like real-time collaboration, easy sharing, cloud saving and access from any device. Users dislike slowdowns and crashes with large datasets, limited advanced features compared to Excel, and weak mobile editing such as dropdowns and line breaks.

pricing.note: Google Sheets is free with a standard Google Account, while Google Workspace plans for businesses are Business Starter at $7.00 per user per month standard (about $3.50 promo for 12 months), Business Standard at $14.00 per user per month standard, Business Plus at $22.00 per user per month, and Enterprise on request.
pricing.extraFees: Gemini AI features in Sheets are metered per month, Business Starter includes no Gemini in Sheets, and Business Standard, Business Plus and Enterprise get different allowances for AI functions and building spreadsheets.

google-sheets.caution: Business Starter has no Gemini AI in Sheets at all, and Gemini features are only included from Business Standard upward. Some advanced integrations and Connected Sheets features are tied to paid Workspace plans, and the free plan has 15 GB shared storage across Google services. Promotional pricing shown in some results applies only for a 12-month term.

description.summary: Google Sheets is a free online spreadsheet program that lets you create, update, and share spreadsheets in real time, from any device with internet. It includes built-in AI help for formulas, insights, and building sheets.
helpsWith: Track a monthly budget with a free template or your own sheet, using formulas to total income and expenses
Share a spreadsheet with an accountant or partner so you can edit together without sending files back and forth
Create charts, pivot tables, and simple dashboards to spot trends in your sales and costs
Get help writing formulas and fixing formula errors with Gemini AI

ai.feature: Gemini in Sheets helps you build tables, write formulas, make charts, and get answers from your data by typing plain requests.

reviews.summary: Users find the interface easy to use, the remote and cloud access convenient, and the integrations and expense tools useful. Users say subscription costs are high and rising, the software has frequent glitches and errors, and support is slow or unhelpful.

pricing.note: QuickBooks Online has a free plan at $0 per month for 1 user, then Simple Start is $38 per month list or $19 per month promo for the first 3 months, Essentials is $85 list or $42.50 promo, Plus is $140 list or $70 promo, and Advanced is $340 list or $170 promo.
pricing.extraFees: Payroll starts at $50 per month plus $7 per employee; card payments on invoices cost 2.99% online, 2.5% in person and 3.5% keyed; ACH bank transfers cost 1%; standard ACH bill pay is $0.50 per payment over monthly allotments; paper checks cost $1.50 each; time tracking add-on is $20 per month plus $10 per user; Bill Pay Premium is $15 per month.

quickbooks-online.caution: The 50% promo lasts only 3 months and does not cover per-employee payroll fees. The free plan has no accountant access and no mobile app or third-party app integrations. Intuit's pricing page shows monthly prices only, so the 10% annual discount mentioned in billing help should be confirmed in your account. Source: saashyre.com

description.summary: QuickBooks Online is online accounting software that tracks money in and out, sorts transactions, and runs reports for a small business. It can also handle invoices, payments, and payroll in one place.
description.howToStart: Start the free 30-day trial on the QuickBooks website, connect your bank account, and you can ask your accountant to join you in the software.

ai.feature: Sorts bank transactions, suggests categories and matches payments, and answers plain-language questions about your books via Intuit Intelligence chat.

reviews.summary: Users like the easy-to-use app, automatic bank connection and expense texts, and helpful support staff who answer questions. Users dislike limited features for multiple states, multiple accounts or complex taxes, slow support responses, required paid subscriptions to file, and a lack of customization for business categories.

pricing.note: Keeper has a Bookkeeping Only plan at $20 a month with no tax filing, plus yearly plans with filing: Standard at $199 a year ($16.58 a month), Premium at $399 a year ($33.25 a month), and Business at $1,199 a year ($99.92 a month) for S-Corps and partnerships, with a 14-day free trial.
pricing.extraFees: Add-on services are charged separately, such as S-Corp return filing at $800, Form 941 at $75, Form 940 at $65, W-2 filing at $75, 1099s at $50 per client setup plus $35 each, and P&L statements at $200; older returns not covered by Premium cost an extra $200 per return.

keeper-tax.caution: The free trial is not a free plan: you are charged the chosen plan after 14 days unless you cancel, and the free trial does not include exporting deductions or submitting a return for IRS filing. The results mention a free version limited to linking bank accounts with limited expense tracking, but the vendor's pricing shows no free plan. Keeper does not document integrations with QuickBooks Online, Xero, NetSuite, Sage Intacct or Microsoft Dynamics, and the results name no other apps it connects with. Capital One only allows viewing the past 90 days of transactions.

description.summary: Keeper is a bookkeeping and tax app that links to your business bank accounts and cards, tracks your expenses and finds deductions as you spend. It can also help you file your federal and state taxes, with a tax pro who reviews and signs your return.
helpsWith: Finds tax deductions automatically from your linked bank and card transactions
Tracks income and expenses and shows a running estimate of your tax bill
Schedules estimated quarterly tax payments on the Premium plan
Files your federal return and up to two state returns, reviewed by a tax pro, with 24/7 AI chat help

ai.feature: Answers tax questions 24/7 via an AI chatbot, and auto-categorizes business expenses pulled from linked bank accounts and cards.

reviews.summary: Reviewers like that the software is easy to use, walks them step by step through filing, identifies deductions, and integrates with QuickBooks. Reviewers complain about high cost, extra fees for state filing and audit support, bugs and incorrect tax figures, and poor customer service that is hard to reach.

pricing.note: TurboTax is priced per tax return, not per month, and the Do It Yourself Premium tier (which covers self-employed income) is listed at $139 federal, rising to $149 late in the season, with state filing extra; a free Free Edition exists only for simple Form 1040 returns with no business income.
pricing.extraFees: State returns cost extra (CNET and Forbes Advisor cite about $64 per state, not confirmed by Intuit); refund processing fee of $40 if deducted from refund; desktop state e-file $25 per state; audit defense and MAX bundle prices are not published.

turbotax.caution: The QuickBooks Self-Employed bundle discount only applies if you start your return by sending data from QuickBooks first; starting in TurboTax first means paying the regular filing price. QuickBooks Self-Employed was discontinued in January 2025 and replaced by QuickBooks Solopreneur (about $20/month), which is a separate subscription. The results do not show a monthly subscription plan for TurboTax itself.

description.summary: TurboTax Self-Employed helps sole proprietors and other self-employed small business owners prepare and file their business taxes online, with access to tax experts who know their industry.

ai.feature: Finds industry-specific deductions and reviews your return for errors, and answers your tax questions with AI-powered Intuit Assist.

reviews.summary: Reviewers like the developer-friendly API, straightforward integration, clear documentation, support for many payment methods, and the easy-to-use interface. Reviewers complain about high and hard-to-understand fees, confusing dashboard and balance screens, slow or hard-to-reach support, and sudden account reviews or fund holds.

pricing.note: Stripe has no monthly plan for a small business; it uses pay-as-you-go pricing with no monthly fee, so the starting monthly cost is $0 plus transaction fees, while Stripe Billing has an annual subscription plan starting at $620 per month or a pay-as-you-go plan at 0.7% of billing volume.
pricing.extraFees: Online domestic card payments cost 2.9% plus 30 cents per transaction; in-person transactions cost 2.7% plus 5 cents; manually keyed cards add 0.5%; international cards add 1.5%; currency conversion adds 1%; ACH Direct Debit costs 0.8% capped at $5; each dispute costs $15; Radar for Fraud Teams starts at $0.05 per screened transaction; Stripe Sigma is $15 per month; Stripe Atlas is a $500 one-time fee; Stripe Tax is 0.5% per transaction; Workflows includes 10,000 steps per month, then about 1.8 cents per step.

stripe.caution: Stripe has no free plan with monthly fees, but the Billing annual subscription requires a 1-year contract; the business.com review lists a Stripe Atlas $500 one-time fee and Stripe Sigma at $15 per month, and the stripe.com pricing page says it has no setup or monthly fees on standard pricing. The integration names QuickBooks, Xero, Salesforce, HubSpot, Shopify and WooCommerce are not named in the search results and are included from general knowledge; the results only mention accounting, CRM and analytics integrations generally via the App Marketplace (business.com, nerdwallet.com, stripe.com).

description.summary: Stripe is an online payment service that lets small businesses accept card and other payments without writing code. It also offers invoicing and payment links that can be shared by email, social media, or text message.
helpsWith: Create a payment link and share it by email, social media, or text message
Send invoices and request payments from specific customers, with automatic reminders
Accept payments in over 40 payment methods and many local currencies
Refund payments from the Stripe Dashboard without code

ai.feature: Uses AI to pick payment methods at checkout, block fraud, retry declined payments, and handle disputes automatically.

reviews.summary: Users like that the system is easy to use, has a simple setup, and makes taking payments and tracking sales simple. Users complain about high transaction fees, extra costs for advanced features, slow or hard-to-reach customer support, and frequent payment holds.

pricing.note: Square Free costs $0 per month per location, Square Plus costs $49 per month per location, and Square Premium costs $149 per month per location, with all three plans including every point-of-sale mode.
pricing.extraFees: Processing fees apply on every sale: Square Free charges 2.6% + 15¢ for tap, dip, or swipe payments and 3.3% + 30¢ online; Square Plus charges 2.5% + 15¢ in person; Square Premium charges 2.4% + 15¢ in person. Manually keyed card sales cost 3.5% + 15¢ on the free plan. Square KDS and Square Kiosk devices carry extra monthly fees on Plus and Premium, and text message overages cost extra. Hardware is sold separately, with contactless and chip readers starting at $59.

square-pos.caution: Square Payroll and Franchise Suite are paid add-ons only, and features cannot be mixed between plans. Square Plus and Premium fees scale with the number of active locations, so unused locations should be deactivated to avoid charges. Phone support on the free plan is limited to the first 90 days, and Square Free subscribers cannot use the Square KDS or Kiosk apps. Pricing details are drawn from squareup.com, squareup.com, and tech.co.

description.summary: Square Point of Sale is a register app that lets a small business take payments in person, online, or over the phone, and see its sales and inventory in one place. It can run on a phone or tablet, and you can add hardware if you want it.
helpsWith: Take payments in person, online, or over the phone, including contactless cards and digital wallets
Accept payments with just your phone using Tap to Pay on iPhone or Tap to Pay on Android
Manage inventory and see low-stock alerts across locations
See sales reports, top-selling items, and customer insights
description.howToStart: Download the Square Point of Sale app from the App Store or Google Play, then sign into your Square account and start taking payments.

ai.feature: Lets owners ask questions about their sales and business data in plain words, and auto-suggests starter catalog items and kitchen categories for their menu setup.

reviews.summary: Users like the easy-to-use interface, the fast payments, the built-in sales tracking and reports, the free app with no monthly fee, and the reliable card readers. Users dislike account holds and fund transfer delays, high transaction fees, poor or slow customer support, missing features such as offline mode and receipt reprinting, and glitches with integrations and hardware.

pricing.note: PayPal Point of Sale has no monthly fee and no plan tiers; the POS app is free to download, and you pay only per transaction plus any hardware you buy (first card reader $29, additional readers $79, terminal $199).
pricing.extraFees: In-person card and QR code payments 2.29% + $0.09; online card payments 2.89% + $0.29 (Expanded Checkout) or 2.99% + $0.49 (Checkout); manually keyed-in card payments 3.49% + $0.09; PayPal and Venmo invoice payments 3.49% + $0.49; virtual terminal payments 3.39% + $0.29; cash transactions have no fee.

paypal-zettle.caution: The $29 first card reader is a new-user price limited to one per business and PayPal can change it at any time; online processing rates are not straightforward; payroll integrations are not offered; sales may be held or delayed for review.

description.summary: PayPal Point of Sale (formerly Zettle) is a system that lets a small business accept in-person card, contactless, and digital wallet payments using a phone, a card reader, or a terminal. It also helps track inventory and sales.
helpsWith: Accept chip, contactless, and digital wallet payments with the app, a Card Reader, or a Terminal
Accept PayPal and Venmo QR code payments
Manage a product list, low-stock alerts, and sales reports
Set up staff accounts and sync with tools like QuickBooks and Shopify
description.howToStart: Sign up for a PayPal business account, download the PayPal POS app, and choose whether to use Tap to Pay on your phone or order a Card Reader or Terminal.

ai.feature: Suggests product recommendations and payment options at checkout, and gives sales trend insights through natural-language requests in the PayPal POS app and developer tools.

reviews.summary: Users find the app easy to use and set up, with receipt capture and automated expense tracking saving time. Users report slow or unreliable receipt matching, confusing navigation, accounting integration problems, frequent logouts and sign-in friction, and poor customer support on Trustpilot.

pricing.note: Free plan costs $0 per user per month, Plus costs $15 per user per month plus a team-size platform fee (save 20% with annual billing), and Enterprise is custom pricing billed annually.
pricing.extraFees: Plus has a platform fee based on team size that Ramp does not publish, 1099 filing is $0.65 per IRS filing (state filing free), and Procurement is an add-on to Plus or Enterprise. Ramp also charges per-transaction fees on ACH and check payments per prismconsultingva.com, and those fees are changing.

ramp.caution: The Plus platform fee is not published, so the true per-user cost depends on team size and needs a sales quote. Free plan integrations are limited to QuickBooks Online and Xero; NetSuite and Sage Intacct require Plus. Sources: ramp.com, stackkite.com, prismconsultingva.com.

description.summary: Ramp is a business finance platform that combines corporate credit cards, bill payment, expense and receipt tracking, and automatic syncing to accounting software. It is built to replace several separate tools a small business would otherwise use.
helpsWith: Issue business cards to employees with spending limits and merchant restrictions set in advance
Capture receipts by phone and match them to card transactions automatically
Route vendor invoices for approval and schedule payments by due date
Sync transactions to QuickBooks, Xero, or NetSuite so books stay current
description.howToStart: Enter your business email on the Ramp sign-up page, complete the application with your business details, EIN, and bank account information, and most businesses are approved within minutes.

ai.feature: Reads and codes expenses and invoices, flags fraud and policy issues, and recommends bill approvals, with a human confirming every payment.

reviews.summary: Reviewers like the easy-to-use interface, strong integrations, fast and accurate reporting, and quick staff training. Reviewers complain about slow and unreliable phone support, frequent glitches, high and hidden fees, and slow refunds.

pricing.note: The Starter Kit is $0 per month for single-location restaurants on one or two terminals, with the Point of Sale plan from $69 per month and Build Your Own quoted by sales, while the retail plan starts at $90 per month.
pricing.extraFees: On the Starter Kit you pay card rates of 3.09% plus 15 cents (Basic), 3.39% plus 15 cents (Core) or 3.69% plus 15 cents (Growth); on Point of Sale the card rate is 2.49% plus 15 cents, or 3.5% plus 15 cents keyed in. Extra terminals carry monthly device fees (for example $50 or $35 per month on Flex terminals and $50 per month on a Go 3 handheld), plus one-time hardware and setup charges such as $250 for virtual installation and $225 for first-day phone support. Payroll in the new restaurant bundle is $9 per employee per month. Add-on prices are quoted privately.

toast-pos.caution: The published prices apply to new customers and single locations only, and the software subscription runs on a 2-year agreement with recurring charges starting at go-live. Toast only works on devices it approves, so you cannot use your own hardware, and the add-ons such as loyalty and marketing are not priced publicly. The source notes Toast offers over 200 integration partners, but only DoorDash, Uber Eats and Grubhub are named in the results.

description.summary: Toast is a point-of-sale system built for restaurants, combining hardware, software and payments in one platform. It handles orders, payments, online ordering, delivery and staff payroll for food businesses.
description.howToStart: Request a free demo on the Toast website or call the number listed there, and a Toast specialist will contact you within 24 hours.

ai.feature: Answers questions about sales, labor, and menu performance, and makes approved changes to menus, stock, and shifts through a chat assistant.

reviews.summary: Users like the easy setup, user-friendly interface, integration with other Zoho apps and e-commerce platforms, and the free plan with affordable pricing. Users dislike limited customization and reporting, missing features and integrations, monthly order limits, occasional bugs and bulk upload glitches, slow customer support, and rising costs as users or Zoho programs are added.

pricing.note: A Free plan exists (50 orders a month, 1 user, 1 location); paid plans are Standard at $29/month, Premium at $79/month, Plus at $129/month and Enterprise at $249/month when billed annually, or $39, $99, $159 and $299 billed monthly.
pricing.extraFees: Prices exclude local taxes. Add-ons: extra user $7.50/month, 500 extra orders $7.50/month, extra location $10/month, 50 advanced autoscans $8/month, Advanced Warehousing $124.17/month (annual billing).

zoho-inventory.caution: The free plan has no barcode generation, stock counting or customer portal, and the 50-order limit is reached quickly by a business with staff. Barcode generation and stock counting require the Premium plan, so a business that scans items should budget $79/month rather than $29.

description.summary: Zoho Inventory is an online inventory management tool that helps a business track stock, orders, and warehouses in one place. It works in a web browser and also has mobile and desktop apps.
helpsWith: Track stock levels across multiple warehouse locations
Create purchase orders to vendors and set reorder points with low stock alerts
Manage sales orders, packing, shipping, and tracking updates
Sell across multiple online channels and keep stock in sync
description.howToStart: Go to the Zoho Inventory website, click Sign Up Now, enter your company name, email, password, country, and phone number, then set up your organization details, or use the free 14-day trial.

ai.feature: Lets you ask questions about stock and orders in plain English, get summaries of overdue invoices, and draft or rewrite written text.

reviews.summary: Users like the wide selection of brands and products, fast shipping, easy website and app use, and helpful customer support. Users dislike unclear extra requirements and verification steps, order cancellations without explanation, slow or hard-to-reach customer service, vendor minimum order amounts, and delays with refunds or wrong items.

pricing.note: Faire is free to join for both retailers and brands, and brands pay only a commission on orders from new retailers found through the marketplace, while retailers can optionally pay for Insider at $19.99 per month after a free 30-day trial.
pricing.extraFees: Brands pay a 15% commission on standard marketplace orders plus a $10 new customer fee on a retailer's first order, and a payment processing fee of 3.5% + $0.30 (next-day payout), 2.4% + $0.30 (30-day payout) or 1.9% + $0.30 (60-day payout); Faire Direct orders carry 0% commission.

faire.caution: Retailer Insider membership renews automatically after the free trial at $19.99 per month unless cancelled, and some retailers may be on an annual plan instead; the Insider program is not available to retailers in Alaska and Hawaii.

description.summary: Faire is an online wholesale marketplace that connects independent retailers with brands. Retailers can browse and buy wholesale products from many brands in one place.
helpsWith: Find products from many independent brands, with filters for order minimums and location
Get free returns within 60 days on a retailer's first order from any new brand
Pay later with net 60 payment terms on eligible orders, so you can stock up now and pay up to 60 days later
Filter for brands with low or no order minimums to try new products with less commitment

ai.feature: Suggests products to retailers through AI-powered ranking, natural-language and image search, and a buying assistant that helps them plan orders.

reviews.summary: Users like the easy-to-use interface, photo-based inventory tracking, barcode and QR scanning, and folder organization. Users dislike the high or unexpected pricing, limited reporting, slow updates and syncing bugs, and weak bulk editing.

pricing.note: Sortly has a free plan with 100 unique items and 1 user license, then Advanced at $24 per month on yearly billing ($49 monthly), Ultra at $74 per month yearly ($149 monthly), Premium at $149 per month yearly ($299 monthly), and Enterprise by quote. sortly.com
pricing.extraFees: Payment is by credit card on paid plans; ACH, wire transfers and Net 30 invoices are only on Enterprise. No per-transaction or per-employee fees appear in the results.

sortly.caution: Paid plans start with a 14-day free trial that requires a credit card and renews automatically at the end of the trial unless cancelled. The 50% yearly discount applies only to the first year of new subscriptions and renews at the standard rate afterward. QuickBooks Online sync for purchase orders is limited to Premium and Enterprise plans. sortly.com

description.summary: Sortly is a mobile inventory app that helps small businesses track supplies, materials, tools, equipment, and products sold to customers, without spreadsheets. It works from a phone, tablet, or computer, with automatic syncing so the team sees the same stock in real time.
helpsWith: Scan barcodes and QR codes with your phone camera to add items and find them quickly
Get low stock alerts when an item drops below a set quantity, so you know when to reorder
Organize items in folders by location, such as a truck and a shop, and see where items are and when they moved
Track equipment and tools and attach photos to show their condition
description.howToStart: Go to the App Store or Google Play, search for "Sortly: Inventory Simplified," install it, then create folders and add your first items by scanning or typing them in.

ai.feature: Suggests reorder points and flags unusual inventory discrepancies to help small businesses avoid stockouts and errors.

reviews.summary: Users say the app saves time on ordering with suppliers, is easy and intuitive to use, and has helpful setup and support staff. Users report the app getting stuck or crashing after an update, suppliers not seeing orders, confusion from receiving orders through several channels, a poor customer support experience, missing catalog items, and a limit on setting prices and minimums by case quantity.

pricing.note: Choco is free for restaurants, while suppliers get a monthly fee based on usage that is quoted by the sales team, and no published monthly dollar amount was found in the results.
pricing.extraFees: Choco CheckOut charges a transaction-based fee, a fixed fee plus a percentage for card payments and a fixed fee only for ACH payments, with no setup costs or monthly minimums.

choco.caution: The results do not show a published monthly price for suppliers, so a small business must request a quote; the free plan applies only to restaurants, not suppliers.

description.summary: Choco is a free app that lets restaurants and cafes place orders with their food distributors in one place, instead of by phone, text, or paper sheets. It sends each order to the supplier in the format they prefer, such as email, text, or direct system integration.
helpsWith: Place orders with many distributors in one app, in about three taps per order, instead of phone calls and paper order sheets
Keep a digital order guide per supplier and check order accuracy, with product IDs, units, and delivery confirmation in one place
Chat with your team and your sales rep in the same app, and see orders across several locations (youtu.be)
description.howToStart: Download Choco from the App Store or Google Play, create a business account with your phone number or email, then add your distributor from the Chats screen and place your first order.

ai.feature: Reads voicemails, texts, emails, and handwritten orders and turns them into clean orders for the business's system, with optional automatic sending.

reviews.summary: Reviewers like the easy-to-use interface, built-in team messaging, and the time saved on scheduling. Reviewers complain about slow loading, app crashes, unreliable notifications, weak phone support, and payroll or billing problems.

pricing.note: The free Comp plan covers 1 location with up to 15 employees; paid Essentials is $44.99 per location per month ($39.99 billed annually), Pro is $89.99 ($79.99 annually), and Premium is $149.99 ($134.99 annually), all per location.
pricing.extraFees: Payroll costs $39.99 per location per month plus $6 per employee paid per month (included with Premium); tip management is $49.99 per location per month on lower plans; some POS providers such as Toast charge their own API fees for the integration; Brink POS integration carries a $10 per location per month fee.

7shifts.caution: Prices are per location and employee caps push a location up a tier when it grows past 15, 30, or 60 staff; figures load dynamically on the vendor page and terms are subject to change, with annual prepayment reported as non-refundable. The product is built for restaurants, so it fits poorly for non-restaurant businesses.

description.summary: 7shifts is a scheduling and HR platform for restaurants that helps owners manage staff schedules, time clocking, tips and payroll in one place. It includes a free plan for basic scheduling and a 14-day trial of all features.
description.howToStart: Create a free 7shifts account on the website, enter your restaurant information, connect your POS and bank account, then invite your employees.

ai.feature: Auto-generates draft weekly staff schedules from past sales and scheduling data, which the owner can edit and publish, and writes a daily AI summary of the manager log, available with the Log Book add-on or a plan upgrade.

reviews.summary: Users like the ease of use, the all-in-one approach to scheduling, time tracking and team communication, and the responsive support team. Users dislike the notification overload, the steep admin setup, the rising cost of higher tiers, recurring bugs, and slow loading on the mobile app.

pricing.note: A Small Business Plan is free for life for up to 10 users with all hubs and features, while paid plans start at $29 per month for the first 30 users on Basic, with Advanced at $49 and Expert at $99 per month, billed yearly or monthly.
pricing.extraFees: No setup or transaction fees are mentioned; extra users cost $0.5 to $4.2 per user per month depending on hub and plan, and the free plan has limits of 1 Time Clock and 1 Job Schedule with archived users counting toward the 10-user cap.

connecteam.caution: The free Small Business Plan only covers up to 10 users, and the free Limited plan covers 10 to 30 users with essentials only; the QuickBooks Online payroll integration does not transfer paid time off, and re-exporting a pay period overwrites hours already in QuickBooks Online. Sources: connecteam.com, besthrtools.com, promptwises.com

description.summary: Connecteam is an all-in-one employee management app for teams who work away from a desk, covering scheduling, time tracking, tasks, training and team communication. For small businesses with up to 10 users, the Small Business Plan is free for life.

ai.feature: Answers employee questions from the company's own knowledge base, auto-builds shift schedules, creates training courses from a topic, converts paper forms into fillable forms, transcribes spoken input, and translates team updates and chats.

reviews.summary: Users like the ease of use, automatic tax filing and withholding, and simple payroll processing that works well with Square's point-of-sale system. Users dislike limited customization and reporting, fewer HR features than larger payroll providers, slow or hard-to-reach customer support, higher costs, and problems with banking info or tax calculations.

pricing.note: Contractor-Only Payroll costs $6 per month per person paid, and Full-Service Payroll costs $35 per month plus $6 per person paid per month.
pricing.extraFees: Paper W-2 or 1099-NEC mailing costs $3 per mailed form annually; Vestwell 401(k) starts at $125 per month plus $8 per participating employee; early wage access costs 1.75% of net pay.

square-payroll.caution: There is no totally free plan, but Square displays a 'Start free trial' prompt whose duration and eligibility are not clearly stated; health insurance premiums and payroll taxes are separate costs. Xero and other accounting platforms need to be verified before purchase. Sources: squareup.com, tech.co, hr.software, gusto.com

description.summary: Square Payroll runs payroll for your team, calculates and withholds taxes, and files federal and state payroll taxes for you. It also creates W-2 and 1099-NEC forms at year's end.

reviews.summary: Users like that the app lets them run payroll from a phone in a few minutes and that it is easy to use, with support agents who were helpful when reached. Users dislike payroll funds being pulled on the wrong day, same-day deposits delayed to Monday, app bugs and freezes, hard-to-reach support with long hold times, and an account setup that was confusing.

pricing.note: Roll by ADP has one plan, listed at $39 per month base fee plus $5 per employee or contractor paid in a month, with a 3-month free trial for new US clients; some pages show $59 base plus $7 per employee instead, so the current rate may differ.
pricing.extraFees: $5 per active W-2 employee or 1099 contractor paid each month; same-day direct deposit or instant transfer carries a per-transaction fee (amount not published); additional companies add monthly and per-employee fees.

roll-by-adp.caution: The free trial is for new US clients only and billing starts after 3 months; you must give 30 days' notice to cancel, and fees may apply during the trial for added services. Pricing shown across pages is inconsistent ($39/$5 versus $59/$7), so confirm the current rate before signing up.

description.summary: Roll by ADP is a payroll app for small businesses that you use by chatting, so you can pay employees and handle payroll tasks in under a minute. It also handles payroll tax calculation, filing, and payment for you.
helpsWith: Run payroll by chatting in the app, in under a minute
Taxes calculated, deducted, filed, and paid for you
Add a new employee or contractor by answering a few chat questions
Give raises and bonuses or run off-cycle payments through the chat
description.howToStart: Sign up on the Roll by ADP website or app and follow the chat-based setup, which takes about 15 minutes or less, using your EIN, business bank details, and employee information.

ai.feature: Lets a small business owner run payroll, ask HR and tax questions, and get business advice by chatting with a generative AI assistant, with alerts and reminders sent automatically.

reviews.summary: Users like the easy-to-use, clean interface, simple payroll runs, and the time saved on everyday tasks like pay stubs, benefits, and time tracking. Users complain about slow customer service and long hold times, app glitches and a cluttered interface, delayed access to pay stubs and real-time bank balance updates, and restrictions on advanced features in higher-tier plans.

pricing.note: Gusto has no free plan; the Simple plan costs $49/mo plus $6/mo per person, the Plus plan costs $80/mo plus $12/mo per person, and the Premium plan costs $180/mo plus $22/mo per person.
pricing.extraFees: Add-ons cost extra: Instant pay $100 per payroll, Same-day pay $90 per payroll, Next-Day pay $15/mo plus $3/mo per person, Remote I-9 $20 per submission, E-Verify $5 per submission, Priority Support $30/mo plus $3/mo per person, Gusto Business Compliance $85/mo per state, Health insurance broker integration $6/mo per eligible employee, HSA $2.50/mo per participant, global contractor payments $5 per payment to US bank accounts, and a $200 annual service charge covers HSA, FSA, dependent care FSA, and commuter benefits.

gusto.caution: Your monthly price rises as you add active employees, and contractors are billed only in months you pay them. Some features like Next-Day pay and Time & Attendance Plus are only included on certain plans.

description.summary: Gusto is a payroll and HR service that runs employee pay, calculates and files payroll taxes, and handles hiring paperwork for small businesses.
helpsWith: Runs payroll and pays employees by direct deposit, with taxes calculated and filed for you
Files federal, state, and local payroll tax forms such as W-2, 1099, 941, and 940
Lets new hires complete their W-4 and I-9 forms online through self-onboarding
Creates job posts, offer letters, and onboarding checklists

ai.feature: Gus answers payroll and HR questions, runs reports, and completes tasks like PTO approvals and salary changes once the owner confirms each one.

reviews.summary: Reviewers like the free job posting, the large number of applicants, the easy-to-use posting process, and the integrations with hiring tools. Reviewers complain about low-quality or unqualified candidates, weak resume conversion and template problems, app bugs and a hard-to-tap interview button, fake or bot applications, and slow customer support.

pricing.note: Employers can post up to three free jobs per calendar month, each live for up to 30 days, and paid Sponsored Jobs (Standard or Premium) have no flat fee and are charged per click or per started application based on a daily budget you set.
pricing.extraFees: No flat upfront fee to post; sponsored jobs are billed by results (per click or per started application) on the first of the month or when the balance reaches $500, and some job types such as relocation or confidential postings may require payment.

indeed.caution: Free job posts are visible for only 30 days and fall back in search results over time, and free-post limits apply only to jobs posted directly on Indeed; the Indeed Smart Sourcing professional plan is listed at $520/month or $4,992/year, and the sources do not name specific third-party applicant tracking systems that integrate with Indeed, so check the indeed.com ATS integrations page for the full list.

description.summary: Indeed is a job search site and hiring tool where employers can post jobs and get applicants. It also lets you find, message, and interview candidates in one place.
helpsWith: Write a job post with help from an AI job description generator, which you can review and edit before publishing
Add screener questions to filter applicants who meet your key requirements
Track, message, and schedule interviews with applicants from your employer dashboard

ai.feature: Drafts job descriptions, sources and ranks candidates, screens applications, and writes outreach messages that the owner reviews and edits.

reviews.summary: Users like that WhatsApp Business is easy to use, offers quick replies and automation, and lets them reach customers on an app they already use. Users complain about limited advanced features, chats getting hard to manage at high volume, app crashes, AI Agent chats getting stuck, poor file and media quality, and no native integrations with many third-party tools.

pricing.note: The WhatsApp Business app is free to download and use, while the WhatsApp Business Platform (API) has no licence fee and charges per delivered message, and Meta One business plans start at US$14.99 a month (Essential, Advanced $49.99, Expert $149, Max $499).
